biography.name: Jules

background.family: Lives with her mother and an older brother; younger cousins visit regularly.
background.finances: Moderate income; education costs and savings are discussed openly.
background.cultureLanguages: English and conversational Spanish within extended family.
background.school: Public high school with biology and craft electives.
background.accessOpportunities: School materials and one permitted dental observation; no treatment experience.

timeline.story: In 2014, Jules liked paper animals and insisted that their legs fit through the doors of a cardboard house. She also enjoyed outdoor chasing games and rarely kept the models once play had ended.

At six, she began building small scenes from reusable packaging. During 2017, she learned that explaining a game to younger cousins worked better when she demonstrated one step at a time instead of repeating the whole explanation.

In 2018, Jules tried school choir and decided she preferred drawing scenery for the performance. She began paying attention to fine details, although rushed homework and forgotten lunch containers still occurred alongside careful hobby projects.

During 2020, she assembled detailed craft models at the kitchen table and helped cousins remember simple routines over video. She liked answering their questions, but did not want every family visit turned into an assignment.

At twelve, biology became more interesting when lessons connected structure with function. In 2023, she repaired a damaged model rather than replacing it, finding the slow reconstruction satisfying even though the first attempt looked visibly uneven.

In 2025, a permitted dental observation made restoring a damaged tooth particularly interesting. Jules watched without providing care, and afterward compared that focused task with broader hospital diagnosis stories she had encountered in school materials.

At sixteen in 2026, Jules is exploring Texas college prerequisites and possible dental school while comparing costs. She prefers building savings to buying a premium car, and she knows neither craft patience nor observation establishes how treatment training would suit her.

ambitions: Compare prerequisites, costs, and dental training
She imagines independent living with savings, familiar people nearby, and time for personal projects.
struggles: Finds interruptions frustrating during delicate work

biography.selfDescription: I liked watching a damaged tooth become something usable again. Making tiny models is familiar; treating a person would be entirely new, so I want to learn more before turning curiosity into a promise.
